newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Geneva expo centre reports strong world interest.
newsitem.headline: Geneva expo centre reports strong world interest.

text.p: Geneva's Palexpo exhibition centre, home to the annual Geneva international car show, reported on Monday it was heading for a total of one million visitors during the first six months of 1997.

Orgexpo, the foundation which manages the expanding centre in a prime location alongside the city's Cointrin international airport, said the attendance figures had confirmed its place among the world's leading exhibition and congress centres.
Opened 15 years ago, Palexpo is increasingly attracting cultural fairs as well as technical exhibitions and major sporting events.
Over 646,000 people, more than one third of them foreigners from 85 countries, visited the car show in March -- which Orgexpo says is the only annual industry event on such a scale.
Palexpo also stages an annual exhibition of inventions, new techniques and products which, together with an orchid show held at the same time in April, pulled in 150,000 visitors.
Geneva's annual International Fair for Books, Press and Multimedia, held in parallel with art and music shows and a special exhibition devoted to the "myth of the Mona Lisa" attracted 119,000 people.
Other exhibitions held so far this year included an international luxury watch fair, Semicon/Europe 97 for the world semiconductor market, and R-97 for the waste recovery and recycling industry.

Events set for the second half of the year include in September Telecom Interactive, organised with the International Telecommunications Union to display on-line services, the fifth annual Second-hand Car show, also in September, an International Antiques Fair in November, and the International Show Jumping competition, part of the equestrian World Cup, in December.
